text:
Kyle Connor is doing what he always does, only louder. He has 19 goals and 32 points in 25 games, on 102 shots, the volume of a winger who plays more than 21 minutes a night and never stops looking for the net. Our wins added, which credits each goal by how much it moved the chance of winning, has him third in the league. Sportsnaut went further, arguing Connor is now covering Winnipeg's biggest problem the way Connor Hellebuyck did for years.

Some of it is finishing. He's at 19 goals on 13.8 expected, shooting 19% against 14% last season, and that rate rarely lasts. But the chances are excellent in their own right, and they're not new: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 66% of his entries last season and getting to the home-plate area in front of the net at an 87th-percentile rate. His last ten games produced 17 points, with his ice time up. Our numbers project about 50 goals, with a range of 42 to 60.
headline: Kyle Connor is shooting the Jets forward
